correctness.rationale: For any adjacent distinct nonzero x,y, the joint orthogonality equations cut out ⟨x,y⟩^⊥ of codimension r because the form is nondegenerate. Exclude zero and exactly those endpoints with self-dot zero. Dependent edges require isotropic scalar multiples and q>2. An AA edge is e_1,e_2. In characteristic two an IA edge is e_1+e_2,e_3; in odd characteristic even the first three coordinates admit an isotropic point: the sets of squares and -1 minus squares each have (q+1)/2 elements, so x^2+y^2=-1 has a solution. Its perpendicular hyperplane cannot be wholly isotropic, since polarization would force it inside its own one-dimensional orthogonal complement. This proves nonconstant multiplicity. For n>=4 all independent edges have at least q^(n-2)-3>=1 common neighbors; dependent edges also have positive counts. In dimension three a totally isotropic 2-space would lie inside its 1-dimensional orthogonal complement, impossible. The ternary isotropic locus has q^2-1 nonzero vectors: in characteristic two the sum of coordinates vanishes; in odd characteristic projectivization is a smooth rational conic with q+1 points (use lines through a rational point, including its single tangent). Counting IA edges from isotropic vertices gives (q^2-1)(q^2-q), and grouping isotropic scalar fibers gives (q+1)binom(q-1,2) dependent edges. The anisotropic degree sum q^2(q-1)(q^2-1) is 2E_AA+E_IA. The resulting three counts multiplied by q-1, q-2 and q^2-3 and divided by three yield the stated triangle product. At (2,3) only the six IA edges have zero multiplicity. `python /workspace/audit_checks_1_5.py 3` independently enumerated graphs using bitset neighborhood intersections for (2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(5,3),(9,3), including F_9 via u^2=-1, obtaining one triangle at (2,3), 56 at (3,3), and 82160 at (9,3). This is regression evidence; the arbitrary-parameter proof is by dimension, not finite extrapolation.

evidence: Godsil states the projective point–hyperplane symmetric design and N²=(k−λ)I+λJ for the polarity-indexed incidence matrix, whose rows record the orthogonality relation including absolute-point loops. Thus diagonal entries count k=(q^(n−1)−1)/(q−1), and distinct rows share λ=(q^(n−2)−1)/(q−1) points, since two distinct polar hyperplanes intersect in a subspace of vector dimension n−2.

Kantor gives the classical common-block-intersection design context. The dot-product graph literature passages on vertex degrees or dimension-two components do not themselves encode the edge intersections.

evidence: The lifted looped adjacency matrix is N⊗J_{q−1}; for two distinct nonzero vectors its common-incidence count is (q−1)k in the same fiber and (q−1)λ in different fibers. For an edge, erasing vertex loops removes ε(x)+ε(y) candidates, giving precisely q^(n−r)−1−ε(x)−ε(y).

Different fibers with an AA or IA edge have values differing by one. In dimension at least four the minimum remains positive after two deletions. In dimension three λ=1 and two distinct adjacent absolute points cannot occur, so only the IA value can vanish, at q=2; the three absolute points have two nonabsolute neighbors each. Counting lifted edges with the usual q+1 absolute points yields the three class counts and their triangle sum.

originality.rationale: Godsil's exact symmetric-design incidence-matrix square, in the same section as the polarity given by the standard coordinate dot product, already determines every two-point intersection of the looped projective relation. The unprojectivized looped relation is obtained by replacing each projective point by its q−1 nonzero vectors, with the same adjacency for every representative, and deleting endpoint loops gives the frozen formula. Thus the finding is a mechanically implied specialization, not an identified verbatim prior vector-level statement. Rank-three counts and the exceptional coverage boundary are immediate consequences with the standard absolute-point count.
residual_risks: The founding Badawi text was not recovered through the attempted lawful route. Orthogonal graphs of odd characteristic and their automorphisms was only identified from indexed material and its full coverage remains unresolved. An earlier verbatim vector-graph formula may occur under additional aliases; the verdict rests on the verified exact projective implication, not either access gap.

value.rationale: The local question is well motivated and the formula is a useful translation of the projective design answer. Under the value standard the exact datum and sharp exception are nevertheless mechanically implied: multiplying the classical projective co-incidence counts by fiber size and removing isotropic endpoint loops yields the entire edge profile. The dimension-three corollaries then use standard absolute-point and degree counts, not a separate mathematical advance.
